Tripwire Interactive lays off workers after announcing new publishing initiative
The Killing Floor studio lays off 36 in a move the former co-founder blames on 'woke leftists' ousting him from his position years ago.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 12, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via Tripwire Interactive
Tripwire Interactive, the Georgia-based developer and publisher behind the Killing Floor and Maneater series, has announced that the company is making 36 jobs redundant, shortly after having just
announced a new publishing initiative for smaller games
.
The Embracer-owned studio
confirmed the layoffs on X
(formerly Twitter) in a statement, reiterating that the studio is continuing work on
Maneater 2
and
Killing Floor 3
, the latter releasing last year but struggling to match its predecessor's numbers. The news comes just days after the company announced
Tripwire Presents
, an initiative that scales publishing duties for smaller games. It is unclear if that initiative was announced with knowledge of impending layoffs, though Tripwire laid off 23 jobs earlier this year
as part of a restructuring plan
.
Tripwire co-founder and former CEO John Gibsonweighed in on this news in response to
a post by game consultant Iain Garner,
disagreeing with the Garner's proposed notion that
Killing Floor 3
was to blame. "This wasn't the issue, it was that woke leftists got me, the CEO, key leader and creative force ousted and the company forced to be sold," Gibson said, referencing his ousting as CEO and
subsequent sale to Embracer
. "This narrative that CEO's are just greedy stuffed shirts is destroyed by this result. The same team that made
KF3
made
KF2
, minus it's [sic] leader."
Related:
One in three developers say they've been laid off within the last two years
Gibson was the head of Tripwire Interactive until 2024,
when he voiced support for Texas' anti-abortion law
, leading to development partners cutting ties with Tripwire Interactive. Thus, Gibson blaming "woke leftists" for his ouster.
"I'm not saying mistakes weren't made following my departure, and I'm not saying I was the only talented person there. I lead a great team of talented individuals, and we succeeded as a team. But pull the linchpin and the machine collapses. Like kicking Steve Jobs out of Apple," Gibson added,
replying to his own tweet
.
